title: Integral scalar square for the normalized proper identity-open comparison
statement: Fix the finite-field datum, coefficient prime and algebraic closure, separated finite-type schemes, proper morphism, normalized ordinary integral comparisons D with their integral laws, normalized compact coefficient action S, and the natural isomorphisms theta of [def-weil-compact-support-coefficient-action] and [lem-sf-strict-direct-image-scalar-comparison]. Assume both the chosen projection equation PreservesProjections and InducedOnFullTower, with the section-normalized identity-open maps. For every coefficient inclusion E <= L and integral constructible K, the map T_Y(theta_E) followed by the inverse ordinary integral comparison equals the compact integral beta followed by theta_L at T_X(K). This is an equality in the integral constructible category before rationalization. Prerequisites: [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], [def-weil-derived-direct-image], [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], [def-weil-compact-support-finite-action], [def-weil-compact-support-coefficient-action], [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], [def-weil-extension-by-zero], [lem-sf-strict-direct-image-scalar-comparison], [def-weil-proper-coefficient-descent-data].

proof.text: Put $F_H=Rf_{!,H}^{c_0}$ and $I_H=Rf_{*,H}$. On every finite quotient write $a_A:(\mathrm{id}_X)_!\cong1$ for the sectionwise identity and $\alpha_A=Rf_{*,A}(a_A)$. The open scalar and restriction comparisons commute with $a_A$: after identifying identity extension by zero with the identity, their sections are $x\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes b$. The ringed-diagram version of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] gives this identity on the full derived coefficient systems, with arbitrary coefficient maps. The given $\theta_H$ is induced by these same identity-open maps on the full defining tower. Thus [lem-weil-proper-integral-tower-comparison] identifies its reduction by $r^H_{*,n}(\theta_H)_n=\alpha_{A_{H,n}}r^H_{!,n}$, retaining the coherent quotient transitions and the actual projection adjuncts.

proof.text:
Fix $E\subset L$, $K$, and $n\ge1$, and put $A=A_{E,n}$, $B=A_{L,n}$, $\eta_X=\eta_{X,n,K}$ and $\rho_!,\rho_*$ for the normalized scalar-restriction maps. By [def-weil-compact-support-coefficient-action] and [lem-weil-strict-direct-image-mixed-unit], the reductions of $b_!$ and $b_*$ are the unique derived tensor-linear lifts through the same mixed source unit. That unit is universal by [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model]. The two reductions of the desired scalar square, followed by the invertible target reduction, have adjuncts
$$\rho_*Rf_{*,A}(\eta_X)\alpha_A r^E_{!,n},\qquad(\operatorname{Res}\alpha_B)\rho_!F_{A}(\eta_X)r^E_{!,n}.$$
Here the first expression uses naturality of the mixed unit with $\theta_E$, and the second uses the projection identity for $\theta_L$ from Step 1. Naturality of $\alpha_A$ with the map $\eta_X$ gives $Rf_{*,A}(\eta_X)\alpha_A=\alpha_{A,\operatorname{Res}(T_XK)_n}F_A(\eta_X)$. The identity-open restriction normalization of Step 1 gives $\rho_*\alpha_{A,\operatorname{Res}(-)}=(\operatorname{Res}\alpha_B)\rho_!$. Hence the adjuncts agree. This calculation takes place on the coherent quotient diagrams: the mixed units and the restriction maps are their actual natural transformations. Universal tensor transposition therefore gives equality of the reduced system maps, including every quotient transition; it is not an inference from separate evaluations.

proof.text: The two original integral maps have source $T_YF_EK$ and target $I_LT_XK$ in the full derived-complete bounded constructible category. Coherent reduction is faithful there by [lem-pod-integral-system-reduction-fully-faithful]. Apply it to the equality of coherent system maps obtained in Step 2, cancelling the target reduction identification: $b_*T_Y(\theta_E)=\theta_LT_X\,b_!$. The same equality with inverses follows by precomposing with $T_Y(\theta_E^{-1})$ and postcomposing with $\theta_L^{-1}$. Thus the comparison and its inverse are compatible with the fixed scalar actions.
